description_overrides.Signal TSH → follicular cell: TSH reaches the blood-facing side of follicular cells and stimulates their thyroid-hormone work. This arrow shows receptor signaling, not passage through a duct; the receptor is not modeled.
description_overrides.Signal 1 Cell makes thyroglobulin: Follicular cells make thyroglobulin, the protein scaffold for thyroid-hormone formation and storage. This marker denotes production; it is not a secretory organelle or a molecular model.
description_overrides.Signal 2 Colloid: Tg + hormone formation: Thyroglobulin enters extracellular colloid at the apical side. Hormone formation/storage is associated with it. The closed follicular lumen has no drainage duct into a blood vessel.
description_overrides.Signal 3 Colloid uptake + processing: The cell takes up stored colloid material at its apical surface and processes it intracellularly. The visible uptake droplets are not lysosomes; lysosomal processing is explained rather than separately modeled.
description_overrides.Signal 4 T3/T4 → blood: After cellular uptake and processing, T4 and some T3 leave the blood-facing side toward local circulation. Thyroglobulin-rich colloid does not drain directly into blood. The arrow abbreviates extracellular transfer.
description_overrides.Signal Calcitonin: C cell → blood: Parafollicular C cells release calcitonin toward local blood vessels. They do not contact colloid. Rising extracellular calcium promotes secretion; calcitonin has a limited role in normal adult human calcium balance.
description_overrides.Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion: CaSR at the chief-cell surface senses extracellular ionized Ca²⁺. Falling calcium reduces receptor activation and favors PTH secretion; rising calcium suppresses it. The sensed ion is not the secreted product.
description_overrides.Signal PTH: chief cell → blood: Parathyroid chief cells release PTH toward their own local circulation. PTH acts systemically to help restore calcium, which then reduces further PTH release. There is no direct vascular link to this thyroid specimen.
description_overrides.Signal symbols enlarged • simplified seq: Enlarged static symbols summarize endocrine relationships. Their arrows give explanatory direction, not tracked molecular paths or speed. Tissue scale is 500 µm per model unit; symbols, thin layers and representative cells are enlarged.
description_overrides.Follicular epithelium: A single layer of follicular cells separates the colloid lumen from the basal lamina and nearby blood supply. The cells make thyroglobulin, deliver it apically to colloid, then recover and process stored material before releasing T3/T4 toward blood. Polygonal bodies are enlarged, simplified representatives; they do not diagnose thyroid activity.
description_overrides.Colloid: Acellular, extracellular thyroglobulin-rich content of the follicular lumen. Thyroid hormones are formed and stored while associated with thyroglobulin; cellular uptake and processing precede release to blood. Translucency is a teaching choice.
description_overrides.Follicular basal lamina: Specialized extracellular support beneath the follicular epithelium, between its basal surface and connective tissue. Distinct from the gland capsule. Authored as complete on all six follicles before the reversible specimen cut; its 2.5 µm modeled thickness is enlarged for teaching.
description_overrides.Intracellular colloid uptake vesicles: Enlarged examples of endocytic colloid droplets near the apical region of follicular cells in three representative follicles. They depict uptake for cellular processing, not marginal empty colloid scallops or a route directly from colloid to blood.
description_overrides.Parafollicular C cells: Distinct calcitonin-secreting cells seated in basal/interfollicular positions, without a colloid-facing surface. Blue is an identification color. The six representative cells illustrate location and release toward local blood, rather than a physiological C-cell abundance.
description_overrides.Thyroid circulation: Local supply, six anastomosing perifollicular vascular beds and drainage, authored as one connected circuit. Red-to-blue color indicates a schematic arterial-to-venous transition, not calculated perfusion or oxygen concentration. External specimen-cut ends are deliberate; internal disconnected ends remain unacceptable.
description_overrides.Parathyroid chief cells: Predominant parathyroid endocrine cells and the principal PTH source. Falling extracellular ionized Ca²⁺ promotes PTH release into nearby blood. Twenty-two enlarged representative cells retain the prior relative arrangement; their shapes and spacing are simplified teaching choices.
description_overrides.Parathyroid circulation: Connected local supply, central vascular course, three side loops and drainage serving the separate parathyroid sample. Two external specimen ends are deliberate. Red-to-blue colors are schematic; no vessel bridge or duct connects this sample to the thyroid specimen.
description_overrides.Follicular cell nuclei: Nuclei inside the enlarged representative follicular cell bodies. These identify the cellular epithelium surrounding the acellular colloid; they are not cells within the lumen.
description_overrides.C-cell nuclei: Nuclei contained within the separately identified basal/interfollicular C-cell bodies. Their enclosing cells secrete calcitonin; neither the nuclei nor the cells belong within colloid.
description_overrides.Interfollicular connective tissue: Supporting tissue between and beneath follicles carries the local circulation. The curved envelope and upper planar face represent a sampled, dissected tissue region; the planar face is an artificial specimen boundary, not a capsule around each follicle.
description_overrides.Capsule: Sampled fibrous gland covering along the lower thyroid specimen boundary. It is separate from follicular basal lamina; the upper exposed boundary is a deliberate specimen cut. This tissue sample does not reconstruct the whole thyroid organ.
description_overrides.Parathyroid capsule: Connective-tissue covering of the separate parathyroid sample. It surrounds a solid cellular glandular region, not a colloid-filled follicle. Thickness and transparency are teaching choices; the review remains unaccepted.
description_overrides.Parathyroid stroma: Connective tissue supporting parathyroid cells and their local vascular passages. Normal parathyroid cells form cords and clusters separated by vascular stroma; this review uses spaced, enlarged representatives rather than a quantitative packing reconstruction.
description_overrides.Oxyphil cells: Larger, mitochondria-rich parathyroid cells, shown here as three enlarged representatives. Mitochondrial abundance helps distinguish them from chief cells. Their endocrine role is not separately simulated; they should not be described as universally inert or incapable of PTH expression.
description_overrides.Parathyroid adipocytes: Three representative unilocular fat cells within the parathyroid sample. Adipose content varies with age and individual context; this small illustrative set does not establish a normal glandular fat fraction.
description_overrides.Parathyroid chief-cell nuclei: Nuclei inside the representative chief cells. Cell bodies and nuclei are distinct, separately selectable parts; modeled size and density are not quantitative histology.
description_overrides.Oxyphil-cell nuclei: Nuclei inside the larger representative oxyphil bodies. Nuclear appearance is simplified; identification also depends on the surrounding mitochondria-rich cytoplasm.
description_overrides.Parathyroid adipocyte nuclei: Peripheral nuclei in the representative fat cells, displaced toward the cell edge by each large lipid droplet. They remain intracellular; the exposed section is a teaching view.
description_overrides.Parathyroid lipid droplets: One large storage droplet within each representative unilocular adipocyte. These are intracellular lipid stores, distinct from colloid and hormone signaling symbols.
description_overrides.Oxyphil mitochondria: A small illustrative set of enlarged mitochondria within oxyphil-cell cytoplasm. It indicates the characteristic mitochondrial enrichment; organelle number, size and arrangement are schematic rather than a quantitative mitochondrial inventory.

states.title: Two tissues, three hormone outputs
states.text: Thyroid follicles show colloid handling, T3/T4 release and C-cell calcitonin secretion. The separate cellular parathyroid shows calcium sensing and PTH release. All arrows are enlarged static teaching symbols.
visible_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: Two sampled tissues are placed together for comparison; their spacing is not whole-organ anatomy.

states.title: Compare tissue organization
states.text: Colloid lies inside thyroid follicles; epithelium and basal lamina surround it. The parathyroid is cellular tissue with its own circulation and no colloid lumen.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: Hiding the schematic group does not remove tissue or alter geometry.

states.title: Input at the blood-facing side
states.text: TSH reaches the blood-facing side of follicular cells and stimulates their thyroid-hormone work. This arrow shows receptor signaling, not passage through a duct; the receptor is not modeled.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: Only the local receiving end is shown; the pituitary and TSH receptor are not modeled.

states.title: 1. Make thyroglobulin
states.text: Follicular cells make thyroglobulin, the protein scaffold for thyroid-hormone formation and storage. This marker denotes production; it is not a secretory organelle or a molecular model.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: Rough endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi and intracellular protein transport are omitted.

states.title: 2. Form and store in colloid
states.text: Thyroglobulin enters extracellular colloid at the apical side. Hormone formation/storage is associated with it. The closed follicular lumen has no drainage duct into a blood vessel.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: This is the approved overview; full iodide/TPO chemistry and molecular geometry are omitted.

states.title: 3. Recover and process
states.text: The cell takes up stored colloid material at its apical surface and processes it intracellularly. The visible uptake droplets are not lysosomes; lysosomal processing is explained rather than separately modeled.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: Existing intracellular uptake droplets stand for selected examples; processing is not a moving-vesicle animation.

states.title: 4. Release toward circulation
states.text: After cellular uptake and processing, T4 and some T3 leave the blood-facing side toward local circulation. Thyroglobulin-rich colloid does not drain directly into blood. The arrow abbreviates extracellular transfer.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: The arrow abbreviates basal release and extracellular access to capillaries; it is not a literal trans-tissue tunnel.

states.title: C-cell secretion
states.text: Parafollicular C cells release calcitonin toward local blood vessels. They do not contact colloid. Rising extracellular calcium promotes secretion; calcitonin has a limited role in normal adult human calcium balance.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: The calcium stimulus is described in text; no additional signal geometry is added.
Do not present PTH and calcitonin as equally dominant adult calcium regulators.

states.title: Sense low extracellular calcium
states.text: CaSR at the chief-cell surface senses extracellular ionized Ca²⁺. Falling calcium reduces receptor activation and favors PTH secretion; rising calcium suppresses it. The sensed ion is not the secreted product.
visible_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
states.focus_part: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: CaSR and downstream signals are explained without adding molecular meshes.
Low is qualitative, not a threshold or simulated concentration.

states.title: Release PTH toward local blood
states.text: Parathyroid chief cells release PTH toward their own local circulation. PTH acts systemically to help restore calcium, which then reduces further PTH release. There is no direct vascular link to this thyroid specimen.
visible_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: Systemic actions are summarized in prose; no bone, kidney, intestine or new vascular bridge is modeled.

states.title: Restored calcium suppresses further PTH
states.text: When systemic PTH actions restore extracellular calcium, stronger chief-cell CaSR activation reduces PTH secretion. The existing low-calcium arrow is hidden in this conceptual comparison; no arrow is reversed.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: This text is a conceptual condition, not a quantitative homeostasis simulator.
No newly added high-calcium Signal part or local return path.

states.title: Off-model thyroid feedback
states.text: Circulating thyroid hormones reduce hypothalamic TRH and pituitary TSH drive. The feedback is systemic; it does not return through the colloid or connect the two displayed specimens.
hidden_parts: Signal Low Ca²⁺ sensed → PTH secretion
limitations: Hypothalamus and pituitary are not represented.
No new feedback arrow or moving hormone particles.

summary: Two separate magnified endocrine tissue specimens. A sectioned thyroid follicle shows extracellular colloid, polarized epithelium and local circulation; a solid parathyroid specimen shows distinct cells and its own circulation. Nine enlarged static schematic callouts teach endocrine input and release.
scale_note: 500 µm per model unit describes the specimen layout. Follicular and parathyroid cells are enlarged/coarsened representatives; basal lamina, vessel walls and organelle examples are simplified or enlarged. Static signaling symbols are not molecularly scaled. The original Thyroid follicles remains separate.
